facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: trimshatsu tri-sahasreshu bharatad ahavad itah | saptabda-sata-yukteshu gateshv abdeshu panchasu
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India documented the 634 CE Meguti temple Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II, which explicitly records that 3,735 years had passed since the Bharata war.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: To the Painted Grey Ware, Period II, a time-bracket of circa 1100 B.C. to circa 800 B.C. may tentatively be assigned.
facts.text: Excavations conducted by the Archaeological Survey of India at Hastinapura dated the Painted Grey Ware settlement layers associated with Mahabharata tradition to circa 1100 BCE to 800 BCE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Excavations at Raja Karna Ka Tila near Kurukshetra exposed a sequence ranging from the Painted Grey Ware period to the late historical era.
facts.text: Excavations by the Archaeological Survey of India at Raja Karna Ka Tila near Kurukshetra identified stratified settlements of the Painted Grey Ware culture dating to the early first millennium BCE.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Astronomical simulations produce dates around 3067 BCE or 3138 BCE, whereas archaeological evidence from PGW sites points to circa 1000 BCE.
facts.text: Archaeo-astronomers calculate that planetary conjunctions and eclipse sequences in the text occurred around 3067 BCE, while mainstream archaeologists maintain that iron-bearing material layers across Kurukshetra sites date no earlier than 1200 BCE to 800 BCE.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: The analysis shows 672 eclipse pairs between 3300 BCE and 700 BCE visible at Kurukshetra, with multiple occurrences of thirteen-day intervals.
facts.source_name: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
facts.text: While researchers attempting astronomical dating claim that paired solar and lunar eclipses within thirteen days define a unique historical event, other astronomers counter that hundreds of thirteen-day eclipse intervals occurred visible over Kurukshetra between 3300 BCE and 700 BCE.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Scholars diverge between the traditional astronomical date of 3102 BCE and archaeological models placing the cultural background between 1500 BCE and 900 BCE.
facts.text: Traditional Indian calendrical reckoning places the Mahabharata war at the threshold of the Kali Yuga around 3102 BCE, while archaeological syntheses propose dates around 1500 BCE to 900 BCE based on settlement patterns and chariot technology.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Local tradition believes that the sacred banyan tree at Jyotisar stands on the exact site of the Gita sermon before the battle.
facts.text: Local folklore at Jyotisar near Kurukshetra identifies an ancient sacred banyan tree as the venerated location where Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita immediately prior to the conflict.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: A dip in the Sarovar during a solar eclipse is believed to carry the merit of performing countless horse sacrifices according to local belief.
facts.text: A long-standing regional tradition asserts that performing sacred ablutions in the Brahma Sarovar at Kurukshetra during a solar eclipse purifies a pilgrim of all demerits.
